skill.name: service-mesh-observability
skill.description: Implement service mesh observability patterns for Istio, Linkerd, Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, Kiali, and OpenTelemetry.
skill.summary: Plan and implement metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alerts for service mesh traffic.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external command findings are Markdown formatting false positives, and the hardcoded documentation or in-cluster URLs are benign examples. The OpenTelemetry template binds telemetry ports to 0.0.0.0, and the Kiali template uses anonymous authentication with broad namespace visibility. No prompt injection text or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Kiali is configured with anonymous authentication and cluster-wide namespace visibility.
remediation.suggestion: Use token or OpenID authentication and limit accessible_namespaces to the required namespaces only.

remediation.issue: OpenTelemetry receivers and exporter bind to 0.0.0.0 in the example configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to expose these ports only inside the cluster and protect them with Kubernetes NetworkPolicy or equivalent controls.

remediation.issue: The Linkerd install example pipes generated manifests directly into kubectl apply.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend version pinning and reviewing generated manifests before applying them to a cluster.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Kiali Dashboard Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The Kiali template sets anonymous authentication and grants visibility across all namespaces. If deployed as written, it can expose mesh topology and workload metadata to unauthorized users.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The YAML explicitly sets auth.strategy to anonymous and accessible_namespaces to ** in the same Kiali configuration block. This is a clear insecure default for shared or production clusters.

content.value_statement: Service mesh teams need clear telemetry patterns to debug latency, errors, and dependencies. This skill provides metrics, tracing, dashboard, and alerting templates for Istio, Linkerd, and OpenTelemetry.
actual_capabilities: Explains service mesh observability concepts and golden signals.
Provides Istio metrics queries for request rate, errors, latency, TCP connections, and request size.
Outlines Jaeger tracing setup for Istio using sampling and collector configuration.
Shows Linkerd viz commands for dashboards, routes, tap output, and service edges.
Includes examples for Kiali topology, OpenTelemetry collectors, and Prometheus alert rules.
limitations: The templates require review before use in production clusters.
It does not inspect a live cluster or verify installed mesh versions by itself.
Dashboard examples are generic and may need labels changed for each environment.
Security settings such as authentication and network policy must be hardened separately.

use_cases.title: Debug Mesh Latency
use_cases.description: Trace slow service calls and compare P99 latency with request rate and error metrics.

use_cases.title: Build Mesh Dashboards
use_cases.description: Create Grafana and Kiali views that show traffic, errors, dependencies, and topology.

use_cases.title: Define Service SLOs
use_cases.description: Choose mesh-level signals and alert thresholds for service communication reliability.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Monitoring
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new service mesh.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic service mesh observability plan for my cluster. Include metrics, dashboards, and alerts for request rate, errors, and latency.

prompt_templates.title: Add Distributed Tracing
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add distributed tracing to an Istio mesh with Jaeger. Explain sampling, trace context, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Latency
prompt_templates.scenario: Incident response for slow service communication.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through debugging high P99 latency between two services in a service mesh. Use metrics, traces, and dependency views.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Observability
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced rollout for a multi-team platform.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production service mesh observability rollout with Prometheus, Grafana, Kiali, OpenTelemetry, SLOs, and security hardening.

output_examples.input: I need to monitor Istio service errors and latency.
output_examples.output: A monitoring plan with Prometheus signal definitions, Grafana panel goals, P99 latency alerts, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: My Linkerd service calls are slow after a deployment.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting sequence using route metrics, live traffic inspection, dependency edges, and trace correlation.
A rollout checklist covering telemetry collection, dashboard ownership, alert thresholds, retention, sampling, and security controls.

best_practices: Start with request rate, error rate, latency, and saturation before adding custom metrics.
Use lower trace sampling in production and keep higher sampling for development or incidents.
Protect dashboards and telemetry endpoints with authentication, authorization, and network policy.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy example dashboards without checking label names and cardinality.
Do not expose Kiali, Grafana, Jaeger, or collector endpoints without access controls.
Do not alert on every metric without clear service ownership and response guidance.

faq.question: Which service meshes does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers common observability patterns for Istio and Linkerd, with examples for Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, Kiali, and OpenTelemetry.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready configuration?
faq.answer: It can provide strong starting templates, but production use requires review for versions, labels, access controls, and network policy.

faq.question: Does it connect to my cluster?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance and templates. Any live cluster checks require explicit user-approved commands.

faq.question: What metrics should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with request rate, error rate, latency percentiles, and saturation. Add service-specific metrics after the baseline is stable.

faq.question: How should tracing be sampled?
faq.answer: Use high sampling in development and lower sampling in production. Increase sampling temporarily during incidents when storage capacity allows.

faq.question: Is anonymous dashboard access safe?
faq.answer: No. Dashboards can expose service topology and operational data. Use authentication and limit access by namespace and role.
